scope: one attended AirDrop photo from a newly configured iPhone to the MacBook Air over the Everyone path
classification: anonymous control: sender and receiver were not signed into the same Apple account

sources: user confirmation that the transfer completed
capture.packetCaptureReason: macOS denied access to the BPF device without elevated privileges

observations.connectionPolicy: distinct TLS connections for Ask and Upload

confirmed: An unrelated iPhone can send to the Mac through the Everyone route without a shared Apple-account identity.
The receiver obtained Ask and waited for explicit user acceptance before the sender opened Upload.
Ask and Upload used separate TCP/TLS flows to the receiver's AirDrop Bonjour port.
The iPhone omitted Hello on this receiver flow.
The successful photo payload used CPIO archiving with adaptive compression.
notConfirmed: Encrypted request headers and plist values were not recovered from the unified log.
The exact adaptive-compression block framing was not visible without plaintext termination or a decrypted packet capture.
This trace does not establish why the same iPhone did not list the espDrop receiver advertisement.
implementationDecision: Retain fresh Upload as the proven iPhone-sender-to-Mac-receiver topology. Do not generalize it to espDrop's reverse sender direction: the anonymous Mac-to-iPhone control reused the accepted Ask TCP/TLS flow.
